purpose: Pre-implementation performance baseline only, not a labeled merchant quality corpus or release-gate result.
runtimePath: Compiled balanceframe.node analyzeDeterministic; no mock, TypeScript fallback, production logic changes or provider calls.

fixtureScope.seed: protocol/fixtures/representative.json canonical legacy ProtocolSnapshot, retained unchanged up to requested size
fixtureScope.phase11ContractFixture: protocol/fixtures/merchant-intelligence.json is a separate synthetic correctness specification; current legacy native API cannot consume its MerchantAnalysisRequest
fixtureScope.qualityLabels: None. Synthetic category assignments are workload input, not adjudicated correct outcomes. No precision, coverage improvement or recurrence quality claims.
fixtureScope.expansion: Preserve all seed transactions unchanged for full-size datasets, including intentional duplicate import IDs. Append deterministic transaction/import IDs that are unique among generated records and cannot collide with seed IDs; retain canonical payee/category records and add generated USD/CAD/GBP accounts with matching balance/transaction currencies.
fixtureScope.generatedOnly: Dates cycle over five years ending at seed snapshot civil date. Absolute Money minor-unit strings exceed the seed maximum and are unique to bound accidental duplicate evidence output; every tenth generated item is inflow, every fifth is uncleared and uncategorized. Remaining categories cycle deterministically. Generated transfers and split children are absent; seed boundary records remain.
fixtureScope.limitations: Small fixed seed payee population and unique amounts do not represent production merchant cardinality, realistic amount distributions or quality. Seed may contain inconsistent payee display names/IDs and excluded-account cases; those observations are not repaired. Calendars, aliases and Phase11 source-field states are not part of this legacy API. No horizon filtering is added to production analysis. Smaller harness sizes use a seed prefix.

measurement.isolation: One fresh subprocess per iteration, serial across both iterations and sizes, inherited taskset affinity of at most two Linux cores. No warmups: every sample is process/native-cold; OS page caches may remain warm.
measurement.latency: performance.now immediately before and after the synchronous native call, including native JSON request parsing, deterministic analysis and native response serialization. Excludes process startup, module loading, fixture expansion, input serialization and JS response parsing.
measurement.deadline: Parent wall-clock deadline covers the complete subprocess, including startup/preparation/native call/response parsing. SIGKILL on timeout, await child exit before another process. First timeout stops that dataset; remaining iterations are explicitly unattempted. Deadline expiry is censored, not a successful latency observation or fabricated exact native duration.
measurement.p95: Nearest rank: sorted sample at ceil(0.95*N). Main p95 elapsed/memory summaries are null unless every requested iteration completes uncensored; completed-only latency p95 is explicitly descriptive, not the full p95. No threshold pass/fail gates.
measurement.memory: process.memoryUsage before/after native call, signed deltas for RSS/heap/external/arrayBuffers, and Linux process.resourceUsage maxRSS converted KiB to bytes before JS response parsing. Returned JSON string remains alive in after snapshot.
measurement.memoryLimitations: RSS delta is an endpoint observation, not peak native allocation or incremental high-water memory. It can be negative due to GC/reclamation. Native Rust allocations are not necessarily represented by V8 heap/external counters. Process lifetime maxRSS includes startup, fixture generation and input serialization, so cannot establish a <=512MiB incremental-analysis-memory gate. Endpoint snapshots cannot sample synchronous native peaks. Per-iteration process isolation removes prior iteration/size allocator carryover, not OS cache or unrelated host load. Timed-out worker peak memory is unavailable.
measurement.scopeLimitations: Not end-to-end Review/Actual SDK/auth/network/UI latency. CPU model/runtime/kernel/affinity, binary/input/fixture SHA256 and account/currency/direction/candidate counts are reported. Affinity is not dedicated hardware, a CPU utilization guarantee or the exact nested cgroup quota; root cpu.max and cgroup membership are informational. Binary optimization profile is not inferred; caller must build release.

knownSourceBottlenecks.finding: All transaction pairs compared, with both merchant names normalized and allocated inside the pair loop; 31,249,875,000 possible pairs at 250000 records before scope filtering.
Each transaction scans a growing prior seen Vec for duplicate candidates: a separate quadratic scan for distinct keys.
Uncategorized candidates scan/normalize known payees; when no exact match, history is scanned/normalized per candidate rather than indexed.

Scoped transactions and history are copied; repeated-merchant names and observed recurrence dates/IDs can retain history-sized vectors. maxResults truncates later in core-protocol and does not bound analysis work or inner evidence.

commandPrerequisites: Use installed compatible Node runtime and release native artifact; enter nix develop if repo dependencies require it. CPU0,1 were available in preparation environment; on another host select any two CPUs from /proc/self/status Cpus_allowed_list. Parent executes commands, no baseline measurements have been claimed by this specification.

currentBenchmark.purpose: Current compiled analyzeMerchantIntelligence over deterministic normalized/admitted synthetic workloads only. Not Actual SDK capture, end-to-end Review, production cardinality or labeled quality evidence. Existing baseline facts, deadlines, cold samples and censored results above remain unchanged.
currentBenchmark.fixturesAndAdmission: Default --workload admitted: reuse baseline expandSnapshot and representative.json with all 22 canonical payees, original Money/date/text/category/cleared facts unchanged. Flatten complete split occurrences; retain parent exclusion semantics. Every member of an account/import-ID group containing contradictory facts is omitted, with explicit omitted IDs/reason/counts. Full reference workloads omit tx_090/091/092/094/095; a_2 tx_093 remains valid. Add deterministic performance-only rows until exactly the requested normalized/admitted transaction count. Report pre-admission/original count, invalid-source omissions and native-cap omissions separately; transactions and affected accounts honestly partial with source truncatedCount for invalid omissions. This is not a workaround in production: Actual SDK capture still fails closed on conflicting source identity.
currentBenchmark.sourceStates: Default admitted workload: canonical importedPayee/notes string/null become present/empty/absent; description/verboseTitle unsupported. Independent pending capability unsupported. Synthetic rows have no tombstone/starting-balance facts; false flags describe this workload only, not an SDK authority claim. Synthetic canonical Money currencies are known, never derived from merchant/name. Horizon is five civil years ending at seed snapshot date, not repaired or shifted. No selected calendar, alias, correction, schedule, provider or generated native rule. Empty legacy rules/schedules are complete synthetic collections; nonempty legacy schedules fail because a faithful typed mapping is unavailable.
currentBenchmark.workloadLimitations: Default admitted workload: generated input is solely performance data, not correct category labels. Existing expansion leaves every generated uncategorized transaction uncleared; these remain ineligible, never flipped to inflate candidate/quality claims. Complete admitted history is still aggregated; selected native suggestions intersect eligible uncategorized IDs and materialize at most 200. All compact nativeRuleClassifications are retained unchanged, independent of explanation pagination. The seed has no rules, so default benchmark compact classification count is genuinely zero; the compiled native correctness test independently proves 228 classifications survive a 200-row explanation page and full 12-outcome history aggregation. Fixed small merchant population, unique generated amounts and synthetic cadence do not represent production or the absent adjudicated corpus.

ruleHeavyWorkloads.selection: Explicit finite --workload names only: wide-or-private-and, broad-account-oneof-and, producer-disjoint-or-and. No rule generation or cleared-state changes occur in the default admitted builder. Each selected stress workload is wholly generated synthetic performance source, not Actual SDK capture, adjudicated category labels or quality evidence; representative.json supplies only its snapshot civil date, and the typed fixture supplies schema/normalization/maxEvidence.
ruleHeavyWorkloads.sizingAndAdmission: For T admitted transactions generate R=min(100000,4*T) legal active source rules: both reference sizes 50000/250000 have exactly 100000 rules; deterministic 240-row smoke has 960. Every generated row is cleared, uncategorized, nonsplit, complete, nonpending, nondeleted, nonstarting and nontransfer with unique stable padded transaction/import/occurrence IDs, matching stable payee ID/name and canonical negative USD Money. Dates cycle over 1825 civil days ending at snapshot date. Imported payee/notes are explicitly absent; description/verboseTitle and independent pending capability unsupported. Entire generated collections and every referenced account/category are declared complete, including empty private/other-account intervals. No omissions or native-cap clipping.
ruleHeavyWorkloads.wide-or-private-and: Half the rules are distinct account-common OR payee-Pi predicates; half are selective payee-Pi AND account-common predicates, all targeting one category. Common account rows match every OR rule plus their own private AND rule. Reference payees=50000, categories=1, accounts=1. Every admitted transaction has a compact classification independent of the 200-row explanation page.
ruleHeavyWorkloads.broad-account-oneof-and: Every duplicate pair shares the single-field account oneOf [account-common,account-private-i] AND predicate. Pair groups cycle target categories 3:1, yielding genuinely weighted multi-ID blocks. First ceil(T/2) rows use the common account: all rules match, authoritative targets conflict, category remains null, and no compact classification is fabricated. Remaining private-account rows match only their own pair and retain its single-category compact classification. Explanations assert exact per-category alternative counts and unique bounded native evidence/contradictions. A separate real-native single-target broad-route test proves all 240 classifications and complete 960-ID matching provenance without pretending mixed targets have a majority winner. Reference payees=32, categories=2, accounts=50001.
ruleHeavyWorkloads.producer-disjoint-or-and: NativeDeepReview producer-shaped source: half account-common OR category-Ci rules, quarter payee-Pi AND account-other rules, quarter category-only-Dj AND rules, all targeting the same category. All common-account uncategorized rows match the broad OR route; both smaller AND contexts are logically disjoint even when a payee posting matches. All category/payee/account references are real declared source resources, never dangling unsupported placeholders. Reference payees=25000, categories=75001, accounts=2. Every admitted transaction has a compact classification independent of explanation pagination.
ruleHeavyWorkloads.schemaAndResourceBounds: Current merchant/2 envelope: <=250000 normalized transactions and <=100000 source rules, payees, categories, account coverage and account/category manifest IDs each; IDs <=256 UTF-8 bytes, text <=4096, opaque rule JSON <=10000 nodes/depth32. These workloads have at most two conditions and two oneOf values, supported Actual normalized field names/types and category set actions. Report full source counts; emitted compact tables may honestly omit source rules unused by any retained classification. No per-row nativeRuleIds/ruleIds expansion, output truncation or coverage caps.
ruleHeavyWorkloads.reportedComplexity: nativeRuleMetrics.sourceRuleCount is all admitted source rules; emittedSourceRuleCount is actual unique IDs in disjoint emitted blocks. rawMembershipCount M is the actual sum of emitted nativeRuleParts.blockIndexes lengths, not source-rule IDs multiplied by rows or expanded matches. partCount counts frozen literal parts, setEdgeCount counts OR references plus all four AND-operand references plus category references, and partAndEdgeCount sums them; the generated workload tests check <=13*T. All tables and every classification are retained once per distinct content hash in each dataset's nativeRuleProofs; every sample and warmup references its complete graph with summary.nativeClassificationsSha256. No provenance is truncated or replaced by counts. Existing request/response bytes and SHA, jsResponseParseMs and p95JsResponseParseMs remain measured and reported separately from serialization+native latency and native peak memory.

currentBenchmark.isolation: One fresh subprocess per dataset, serial sizes/calls, same-process 2 warmups then 20 samples. Child uses --expose-gc. Module/fixture/source mapping prepared outside timing; request JSON is serialized on every measured call. Warm allocator reuse differs from old process-cold/no-warmup baseline; neither CPU affinity nor OS cache state guarantees dedicated or identical hardware.
currentBenchmark.latency: elapsedMs is measured JS source-input JSON serialization plus synchronous N-API call. Native call includes request string conversion/native JSON parsing, analysis and full response serialization/return conversion. Report native and JS serialization p95 separately; JS response JSON parsing separately and excluded from native/serialization gate. Preparation, GC, request hashing, kernel measurement reads, correctness summaries and IPC are outside latency timing. Not a Review/SDK/auth/network/store/UI latency claim.
currentBenchmark.memory: After serialized input and explicit GC, worker enters a phase/iteration-bound pre-native IPC barrier. Parent SIGSTOPs its existing owned child, verifies every /proc/PID/task thread and leader are T, preserves sorted TID membership and checks stat thread count. Read status VmRSS R and stat field24 fast RSS F using the actual getconf PAGESIZE; require PID/starttime/thread count/F/R stable across writing 5 to /proc/PID/clear_refs. Require EXACT reset HWM=max(F,R), not HWM=R: the exported-counter reset model accounts for fast versus full-sum counters without any byte/page tolerance. Parent resumes child in finally and releases barrier. Worker retains raw response and enters a second barrier BEFORE JSON.parse; parent again stops and verifies stable membership/counters, reads fresh HWM/current RSS WITHOUT reset, resumes in finally and releases parsing. Metric is approximate exported post-call HWM minus verified full/status baseline RSS R. Any positive initial F-R contributes unchanged; never subtract that bias to improve a gate. Observation allocations happen in parent, not measured child; IPC/control allocations between reset and final stopped observation contribute. Report page size, PID/starttime/thread count, F/R/expected reset HWM/initial counter excess, observer/all-thread-stop proof, deferred parse, absolute RSS/HWM and endpoint delta separately. Unsupported/denied/unstable/reset/read/resume failures are unproven with null peak, never endpoint/lifetime fallback. Existing deadline remains armed throughout checkpoint waits. All20 complete samples must have verified exported-counter increments <=512MiB; maximum, not p95 memory, governs.
currentBenchmark.memoryLimitations: Kernel stat RSS and status RSS/HWM are approximate counters, not exact physical/native allocation accounting or a proven physical-RSS upper bound. Proven means the exported-counter reset and checkpoint model verified, not exact physical memory. Prepared inputs/module loading/pre-window GC/warm allocator residency are baseline costs; final permission delivery, response parsing and correctness/report generation remain outside the native window. A stopped external observer removes self-read allocation/GC perturbations, but observed T states and stable counters are not an atomic kernel-accounting snapshot. Earlier self-observed and parent-observed artifacts, including strict HWM=VmRSS reset failures, retain their original null peaks/unproven gates; no historical reclassification. Matching installed mm.h confirms fast reset assignment; upstream proc implementation is supporting evidence, not identical local kernel source. An owned-child diagnostic established20 stable F<R resets, each lowering inherited high water to exact max(F,R); this alone does not explain historical F>R failures. Sources: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_clear_refs.5.html ; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_status.5.html ; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/proc_pid_stat.5.html ; https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man7/signal.7.html ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/fs/proc/task_mmu.c ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/torvalds/linux/master/fs/proc/array.c (not a claim identical local kernel source).
currentBenchmark.gates: Nearest-rank p95 of serialization+native <=2000ms at 50000 and <=5000ms at 250000. Only exactly 20 complete uncensored samples following >=2 completed warmups establish a reference gate; memory additionally requires all 20 verified high-water windows <=512MiB. Incomplete, censored or unproven reference gates exit2 after retaining JSON; failed gates also exit2. Smaller smoke datasets are descriptive/not_applicable, never release evidence. First deadline kills and awaits subprocess exit before next size; samples/warmups/preparation censoring and unattempted work reported honestly.
currentBenchmark.identityAndOutput: Report actual Node/runtime/architecture/kernel/CPU/affinity/cgroups, request SHA/bytes, both fixture SHA values, addon SHA, generator/mapping version and source-code SHA values, full response SHA/bytes, complete source coverage/counts, native candidate/page counts and every compact native classification. Complete nativeRuleProofs are content-addressed per dataset and shared across identical samples/warmups instead of repeated in IPC and artifact JSON; different graphs remain independently preserved. Native calls still serialize and return every classification on every measured invocation. Earlier reference Node v24.11.1 is recorded separately; current process.version is always reported and runtime identity discrepancy explicit. Build optimization profile cannot be inferred. --output creates a new mode0600 artifact exclusively (never overwrites); stdout otherwise contains complete JSON with no shell truncation.
currentBenchmark.executionOwnership: Parent only, serial on two allowed CPUs, using real compiled addon and installed compatible Node. Replace NEW with an unused artifact path; read the complete artifact with the file tool. No current performance values or passing release/quality/Review gates claimed by this specification.
